member_002 (independent reviewer) here. I've independently located the bug location so I can review your fix efficiently.

Root cause hypothesis: in src/_pytest/capture.py, FDCaptureBinary.__init__ builds an EncodedFile (subclass of io.TextIOWrapper) with only encoding/errors/write_through and NO newline argument. Default newline=None causes universal-newline translation on write, so '\r' and '\r\n' become '\n'. Compare CaptureIO which explicitly passes newline="".

Expected fix: pass newline="" to that TextIOWrapper/EncodedFile so carriage returns are preserved for capfd.readouterr(). Please also verify sys-capture (capsys) and add/adjust a public regression test in testing/test_capture.py (e.g. test_capfd_includes_carriage_return).

I have NOT edited anything in my tree. Please publish your final candidate with fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and send me handoff_patch; then I will integrate_patch, run_tests on your exact version, and org_review_patch accept/request_changes. Do not run submit_integration until I accept.

Final candidate patch-1 is published for your independent review (issue #7521: capfd.readouterr() converts '\r' to '\n').

Your root-cause hypothesis was correct: FDCaptureBinary built its EncodedFile (io.TextIOWrapper) without a newline argument, so the default newline=None applied universal-newline translation to written data, turning '\r' and '\r\n' into '\n'. CaptureIO already passed newline="".

Contents of patch-1 (source version v6, base v1):
1) src/_pytest/capture.py: added newline="" to the EncodedFile(...) construction inside FDCaptureBinary.__init__ (right after errors="replace", before write_through=True). This disables newline translation on write.
2) testing/test_capture.py: new regression test TestFDCapture::test_writeorg_newline (inserted after test_writeorg) — starts capture.FDCapture(1), writes "hello\r\n", snaps, asserts the captured text == "hello\r\n".
3) changelog/7521.bugfix.rst: changelog entry.

My own same-version evidence (v6): focused run of TestFDCapture, TestStdCaptureFD, test_capture_binary_output, test_encodedfile_writelines => 25 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.

Please integrate_patch patch-1, run public tests on that exact adopted content, and then org_review_patch accept or request_changes. Files changed: src/_pytest/capture.py, testing/test_capture.py, changelog/7521.bugfix.rst.

Independent review of patch-1 is ACCEPTED (review-1, event 48). No changes requested.

What I did independently on your exact candidate:
1. integrate_patch(patch-1) into my private tree -> version v2, files_sha256 e6c9e84f17e826f59e8d5262e2c1e9f13c0a8262dd65dced230edeb92e6b51cd, 3 paths, 0 conflicts.
2. Inspected the actual adopted diff: only the single functional line `newline=""` added to the EncodedFile in FDCaptureBinary.__init__ (matching CaptureIO's existing newline=""), plus regression test TestFDCapture::test_writeorg_newline and changelog/7521.bugfix.rst. Minimal and correctly targeted at the root cause (default newline=None universal-newline translation \r and \r\n -> \n).
3. Ran public tests on v2:
   - Focused (report test-report-9067e1f1c139f6a4d83de2d5): 3/3 passed, including test_writeorg_newline which asserts "hello\r\n" survives intact (the issue's reproducer shape `out.endswith('\r')`), plus pre-existing test_writeorg and test_capture_binary_output.
   - Full testing/test_capture.py (report test-report-d0ea0cb7e82a1e99a53b3a9c): 117 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xfailed, 6 failed. All 6 failures are pytester fnmatch/assertion-format mismatches on nested sub-run output (e.g. actual 'E       cannot use capfd and capsys at the same time' vs expected 'E * cannot use capfd...'), i.e. a pre-existing artifact of this pytest version's error formatting, unrelated to newline/carriage-return handling and not caused by your change.

Over to you as delivery member: explicitly integrate patch-1 in your own tree, run_tests on that exact final version, fix_patch(task_ids=[]), then submit_integration. Note the 6 pytester format failures above are environmental and pre-existing; they are not newline-related regressions, but they may still show in your full-suite evidence, so mention them in your submission message.

Please adopt, run public tests, and review this final candidate: patch-2 (issue #7521 fix).

Content is identical to the patch-1 you already accepted: files_sha256 e6c9e84f17e826f59e8d5262e2c1e9f13c0a8262dd65dced230edeb92e6b51cd, 3 paths (src/_pytest/capture.py, testing/test_capture.py, changelog/7521.bugfix.rst).

Current-version evidence on my side (v8): focused run of TestFDCapture + TestStdCaptureFD + binary/fixture capture tests = 27 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed (report test-report-a7693b7cf5bd47db575dadd7). The regression test TestFDCapture::test_writeorg_newline passes.

One caveat worth noting for your review: a full-file testing/test_capture.py run shows 6 failures, but they are all testdir.runpytest() OUTPUT-FORMAT assertions (test_capsysbinary, test_capturing_getfixturevalue, test_disabled_capture_fixture). The inner spawned tests actually pass; the outer assertions fail because the harness injects a PytestAssertRewriteWarning for plugin pws_public_test_evidence_v141 into subprocess stdout and differs in 'E ' indentation. This is environmental, not from the newline change. Please verify independently.
